phrases.text: This narrow strip of water can shake the entire world economy.
At its narrowest, it's less than forty kilometres wide.
And the shipping lanes? Just a few kilometres each way.
Yet every single day, around a fifth of the world's oil passes through here.
Tankers leaving Saudi Arabia, Iraq, Kuwait, Qatar and the Emirates all funnel through this one gap,
with Iran on one side, and Oman on the other.
If it ever closed, oil prices around the world would surge.
That's why this tiny strait is one of the most watched places on Earth.
